extracted.intended_audience: sovereign issuer officials: investor relations officers (IROs), finance ministries, central banks, debt management offices, and other public finance policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Voluntary best-practice guidelines for sovereign investor relations programs (IRPs), describing institutional setup, communications channels, data dissemination, ESG disclosure, transparency of debt information, and conduct during market stress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated Investor Relations Office (IRO) and Officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a designated IRO and an Investor Relations Officer as the first formal point of contact — a one-stop shop for investors and authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Location of the office is flexible (Treasury, Central Bank, Ministry of Finance). The IRO should provide relevant data from across official sources and enable investor access to policymakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRO staff: facilitate two-way communication
rubrics_metrics.description: IRO staff should facilitate two-way communication channels with investors through email, conference calls, and the IR website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Channels must enable investors to ask questions and give feedback; maintain lists and schedules to support routine and ad-hoc engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRO staff: brief senior policymakers on market feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: IRO staff should brief senior policymakers on market feedback, overall market sentiment by asset class and global context, and anticipated market reactions to policy changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular synthesis of investor sentiment helps policymakers calibrate communications and policy choices; include expected market impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRO staff: disseminate macroeconomic data and answer queries
rubrics_metrics.description: IRO staff should disseminate relevant macroeconomic data and policy information to market participants and respond to questions about the data and related issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate distribution via website and email lists; ensure explanations and methodological notes accompany data as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRO staff: disseminate ESG data and answer queries
rubrics_metrics.description: IRO staff should disseminate relevant ESG data and policy information and answer investor questions about policies, plans, financing needs, and related issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include commitments, targets, forecasts, and documentation supporting ESG-related instruments and programmes.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRO staff: coordinate access to data and government officials
rubrics_metrics.description: IRO should coordinate access to data/information from official institutions and develop cross-agency networks who can answer investor queries and consult on policies/regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build a roster of agency contacts and procedures for timely interagency responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRO staff: coordinate investor access to senior policymakers
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate market participants' access to senior policymakers, particularly during times of stress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure senior officials are available for teleconferences, roadshows, or bilateral meetings when needed; maintain escalation procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRO staff: coordinate and present a unified interagency message
rubrics_metrics.description: IRO should coordinate the country’s interagency message and convey a streamlined, coherent explanation of policies and data changes to investors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present coordinated explanations for policy shifts; align messaging across ministries/central bank/debt office to avoid conflicting statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRO staff: maintain credibility by acknowledging weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain credibility at investor briefings by acknowledging policy weaknesses and economic concerns when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Honest acknowledgment reduces surprise and builds trust; avoid over-optimistic or evasive messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRO staff: manage relationships with credit and ESG rating agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Proactively manage relationships with credit and ESG rating agencies, understanding methodologies and engaging to bridge information gaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular engagement can prevent misinterpretation of policy or data; be prepared to explain assumptions and methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRO staff: coordinate with Primary Dealers
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate with Primary Dealers (PDs) as channels between sovereign debt managers and investors in the primary market to support IR efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active PD engagement supports market outreach and helps disseminate issuance plans and market feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRO governance: proximity to senior policymakers and insulation from politics
rubrics_metrics.description: IROs should be proximate to senior policymakers for access and influence, while also being insulated from short-term political changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commitment at the highest level is crucial; institutional design should protect continuity of IR functions across administrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRO staffing skills and market familiarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Core staff should understand market practices, economic and ESG policies, and be able to articulate these to policymakers and investors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular investor contact and use of external market sources help build a 'fabric of trust' and inform communications strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dedicated IR website (bilingual)
rubrics_metrics.description: Countries should host a dedicated IR website regularly updated in the local language and English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Website is the central vehicle for conveying policy objectives, collecting feedback, archiving materials, and providing investor registration/contact functionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: IR website: clear, concise, user-friendly presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: IR website must present concise information in a simple, well-organized, user-friendly format with easy navigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid clutter; prioritize investor-relevant content and logical menus/archives; include FAQs and contact details.

rubrics_metrics.name: IR website: essential functional components
rubrics_metrics.description: IR website should include economic and ESG data/policies, advanced search, archived presentations/audio-video of teleconferences, links to official agencies, investor registration, FAQs, and contact information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure archived streaming, downloadable materials, and reciprocal links to agency sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely and regular dissemination of data and policy information
rubrics_metrics.description: Disseminate up-to-date data and policy information on a timely and regular basis using a release calendar to notify markets of upcoming releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Release calendar helps dispel speculation; maintain cadence even during stress (do not reduce frequency).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide specific, tailored interpretations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide specific, tailored interpretations rather than broad generalities, especially when information flow is negative or during periods of market stress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextualize data, explain policy implications, and outline scenarios to help investors interpret developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Machine-readable and user-manipulable data formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide data in machine-readable formats (e.g., Excel, APIs) rather than primarily PDFs/Word, and include time series of at least two years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enable investors to specify parameters (time period, currency) and download tailor-made time series; quality of data that investors use is preferred over volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose changes in definitions and data revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Inform investors proactively of any changes in technical definitions or data revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer methodological notes and justification to preserve interpretability and comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination of core statistics quarterly (IMF SDDS/SDDS Plus encouragement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disseminate core statistics for fundamental analysis (real sector, fiscal, external, financial sector statistics) quarterly following international standards (IMF SDDS encouraged).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include methodological notes and an indexed archive or links to hosting agencies; countries encouraged to subscribe to SDDS Plus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination of Financial Soundness Indicators (FSIs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report FSIs as identified by the IMF, including core and additional sets for deposit takers, real estate, money market funds, insurance, pensions, nonfinancial corporations, households.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FSIs provide insights into linkages between financial and real sectors and should be part of regular data dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide forward-looking information on economic policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Disseminate forward-looking information such as budget projections, monetary policy targets, structural factors, debt management strategy, annual borrowing plans, and issuance calendars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include assessments of environmental impacts of budgetary/fiscal policies where appropriate and maintain indexed archives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget operations and central government debt transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose central government operations, debt management strategy, annual borrowing plans, issuance calendar, rationale for planned borrowing, and ex-post assessments of public debt operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget transparency is core to debt sustainability analysis; timely tracking helps investors make informed decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive disclosure of central government debt liabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Disseminate information reflecting central government liabilities comprehensively and, where relevant, debt of entities guaranteed by the central government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure helps identify fiscal risks under different scenarios early.

rubrics_metrics.name: External debt transparency and resident/non-resident holdings
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide availability of assets and liabilities of private and public sectors held by non-residents and resident holdings of external debt to help assess international position and balance-sheet vulnerabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include data that enable proper assessment of exposure to external shocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader debt stock coverage (granular categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose broader debt stock coverage beyond central government: publicly guaranteed debt, local/state government debt, SOE debt, off-balance-sheet liabilities (PPPs, pension obligations, central bank repos/swap lines), collateralized/resource-backed debt, and long-term trade credits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Granular coverage supports credibility of fiscal plans and market confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creditor and currency composition of public external debt
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose creditor and currency composition of public external debt by instrument for domestic and external debt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed breakdowns assist investors in understanding rollover, currency and creditor concentration risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debt service profile by creditor and instrument
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide debt service profiles broken down by creditor and instrument for both domestic and external debt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Debt service profiles are critical for assessing near- and medium-term repayment burdens and liquidity risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterly dissemination of debt stock at different valuations
rubrics_metrics.description: Disseminate debt stock and debt service profiles on a quarterly frequency; dissemination at nominal, market and face values is strongly encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple valuation measures improve assessments of debt sustainability and market risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicly accessible database of bond prospectuses and transaction-level terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a public database of domestic and external bond prospectuses and release key financial/legal terms of project-related and other loan contracts with external creditors; consider publishing transaction-level information per IIF/OECD information matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public disclosure of transaction-level data improves debt sustainability assessment and debtor credibility; confidentiality clauses in private agreements may constrain this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely dissemination of ESG policies and progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a timely flow of information on governments’ ESG policies and progress, including commitments under international agreements, SDGs, and domestic sustainability objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display climate commitments, targets, forecasts, scenarios and outcomes clearly and promptly on the IR website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish framework legislation and logs for GSS issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish framework legislation articulating sustainability objectives and the role of green/social/sustainable (GSS) bond and loan issuances; maintain a log of GSS issuance and supporting documentation (prospectuses, reporting on eligible projects, planned allocations, impact and third‑party verification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide verification materials and reporting to enable investor assessment of claims and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish national green/social taxonomies
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish national green or social taxonomies and explain their role in supporting the greening of domestic financial systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taxonomies help standardize what qualifies as green/social investments and inform investor decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose broader ESG-related plans and budget-level reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose other plans and policies supporting ESG priorities, including NDCs, net-zero targets, adaptation priorities, funding needs, accounting of climate and natural capital risks, and budget-level climate/social expenditures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link fiscal policies and budget lines to climate/social objectives for investor assessment of fiscal exposure and commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain and update a comprehensive investor contact list
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and maintain an up-to-date comprehensive contact list of investors, analysts, rating agencies, and other market participants, including institutions with key local relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly update and segment the list to know who investors are and to anticipate creditor behaviour in times of vulnerability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish formal feedback and communication channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Create formal, regular channels for investor questions and feedback to inform policymakers—teleconferences/webcasts, conferences/workshops, bilateral meetings, phone/email contacts, interactive roadshows, and social media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Channels should enable structured feedback loops and ensure investor input reaches key policymakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teleconferences/webcasts: senior-led, regular, archived, and leveled
rubrics_metrics.description: Hold teleconferences/webcasts led by senior decision makers (e.g., undersecretary of finance, central bank deputy governor) at least quarterly; provide advance materials, record sessions for replay, and archive associated materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alert investors by email in advance; present uncomplicated, forward-looking material; provide the same information to all investors simultaneously to ensure a level playing field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Face-to-face interaction and non-deal roadshows
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide bilateral meetings with senior policymakers and conduct interactive non-deal roadshows (semi-annual or as opportunities arise) to foster dialogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-deal roadshows are especially important during challenges; ensure IRO staff can arrange and follow up on meeting requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure investor-oriented presentations and language
rubrics_metrics.description: Policymakers and IR staff should communicate in the 'language' of investors, making presentations uncomplicated and forward-looking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor content to investor sophistication; avoid excessive technicalities in broad outreach but be prepared to provide technical detail when requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Escalation and intensified engagement during diminishing market confidence
rubrics_metrics.description: When market confidence diminishes, intensify consultations with investors, increase frequency of teleconferences/webcasts and direct engagement, and involve senior policymakers to add credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain or increase the frequency of data/policy dissemination; use senior-led roadshows and direct dialogues to clarify rationale for measures and show readiness to incorporate market feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual self-assessment, benchmarking and use of investor surveys/consultants
rubrics_metrics.description: IROs should conduct annual assessments of service quality (timeliness, accuracy, relevance, reach, feedback processing, technology use) and can benchmark against IIF best practices or use outside consultants (e.g., SIRAS) and investor surveys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use self-assessments, external reviews and investor surveys to identify gaps and improve IR practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate press relations from investor relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep press and IR functions separate due to different audiences, content needs and staff skill sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investors require technical, market-relevant, forward-looking information tailored for creditor decision-making; press needs big-picture messaging and public-relations skills. Co-mingling can dilute specialized responses.
